title: dedicated: autoscaler burst smoothing + improved fleet utilization reporting
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: Fleet autoscaling for Dedicated deployments has shown oscillatory behavior during sudden traffic bursts. This leads to temporary overprovisioning and then rapid scale-downs that momentarily violate throughput guarantees. We need a smoother burst control path and richer utilization reporting so SRE/product can observe and tune policies.

What this PR does: Implements a token-bucket based burst smoothing layer in the dedicated autoscaler and extends utilization reporting to emit per-fleet, per-priority, and windowed (1m/5m/15m) utilization metrics. The smoothing layer reduces scale-up/scale-down churn by limiting effective burst credits and adding an exponential decay on outstanding burst tokens. Reporting changes include new metrics (dedicated.fleet.utilization, dedicated.fleet.burst_credit, dedicated.fleet.queue_depth) and an update to the reporting pipeline to backfill recent samples for dashboards.

Design notes: The burst smoother sits between admission control and the autoscaler decision function. It maintains a token-bucket per-priority class; tokens are replenished at configured rates and consumed on incoming requests above baseline capacity. Autoscaler decisions now consider the smoother's effective demand signal instead of raw instantaneous demand. Metrics are emitted with labels: fleet_id, region, priority, and rollout_tag. We added feature flags (env var REDWOOD_AUTOSCALER_BURST_SMOOTHING=true, REDWOOD_UTIL_REPORT_V2=true) to allow staged rollout.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag off in main, run canary with smoothing enabled on single low-traffic fleet. 2) Monitor new metrics and SLO dashboards for 24h. 3) Gradual rollout to fleets with high burst variance. 4) If regressions observed, flip feature flag off for affected fleets; autoscaler will revert to previous signal.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for smoother token logic and decay - [x] Integration test for autoscaler decision path - [x] Metric definitions and dashboard draft - [x] Load test verifying reduced oscillation and preserved throughput guarantees - [x] Docs update for dedicated autoscaler config and flags

Related: ENG-3421, SRE-114, linked support ticket SUP-78.
commits: feat(autoscaler): add token-bucket burst smoothing layer
perf(autoscaler): use decayed burst tokens in scale decisions
pipeline: backfill recent utilization samples for v2 reporting
tests: add unit/integration tests for burst smoothing
review_comments: Evan Park: Can you explain why we chose token-bucket vs EWMA smoothing? Concern is tail latency when burst tokens are exhausted.
Maya Thompson: Token-bucket gives explicit credit accounting which matches our burst SLAs; we added a small EWMA on request rate for the baseline signal to protect tail latency when tokens run out.
Rashmi Patel: Please add a safety check to avoid negative token values and a max token cap based on fleet size.
Maya Thompson: Added cap and clamped values in token_bucket.rs (see commit 3). Also added unit tests covering cap behavior.
Liam O'Connor: CI flaked on pipeline unit job previously, re-ran and it passed. Approving after test fix.
Evan Park: Left a nit on metric label naming; please make sure labels follow 'fleet_id' and not 'fleet' to stay consistent.
Maya Thompson: Fixed labels in metrics definitions and updated dashboards.
release_notes:
- Autoscaler: Add burst smoothing (token-bucket) to reduce scale churn during traffic spikes.
- Observability: Emit v2 utilization metrics per-fleet and per-priority (1m/5m/15m windows).
- Backfill: Reporting pipeline now backfills recent samples for dashboard continuity.
testing_notes: Load tests show 35% reduction in scale-up/scale-down cycles across high-variance workloads and <5% CPU overhead. Canary on test-fleet ran for 48h with no SLO regressions. Integration tests include simulated burst replay and token exhaustion scenarios.
